text:
maria: Quick heads-up — running `terraform apply` for staging-network after importing some k8s secrets. The apply is timing out during the k8s provider refresh and plan shows a replace for a ConfigMap and a tainted Deployment.

maria: here's the error I see during apply:
```
Error: 1 error occurred:
	* provider "kubernetes" encountered an error while refreshing state: Get "https://10.0.0.1/api/v1/namespaces/staging/configmaps/my-config": dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: i/o timeout
```

kevin: pinging infra oncall, but also did you run `terraform state show` for the configmap?

maria: yes — `terraform state show kubernetes_config_map.my_config` returns an empty provider_id and metadata shows owner_references from a Helm release applied earlier out-of-band.

sara: @maria can you paste the plan diff snippet? curious what fields are changing.

maria: plan shows:
```
# kubernetes_config_map.my_config will be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_config_map" "my_config" {
    metadata {
      name = "my-config"
      namespace = "staging"
+     annotations = {
+        "app.kubernetes.io/managed-by" = "terraform"
+     }
    }
}
```

tom: Hm. If the configmap was created by Helm and has ownerReferences, k8s API may reject updates depending on permissions. Also immutable configmaps/secrets can cause errors.

kevin: did anyone check `kubectl get cm my-config -n staging -o yaml`? Maybe `immutable: true` or different annotations.

maria: yep, output shows `immutable: true` set (was set by app team to prevent accidental updates).

sara: That would explain the replace + API timeout. The k8s API will refuse patching immutable objects and if TF tries to do a delete/create while the resource is owned by Helm, it can hang or be blocked by finalizers.

maria: To confirm I tried `terraform import kubernetes_config_map.my_config staging/my-config` — import succeeded, but `terraform plan` still wants to replace because immutable remains true and owner_references differ.

tom: Two options: coordinate with app team to toggle `immutable` off and let TF update, or change TF to use `kubernetes_manifest` (server-side apply) or adopt the resource out of Helm. Another short fix: set lifecycle.ignore_changes for metadata.annotations while you reconcile.

kevin: If you go the import + adopt route, ensure provider alias matches the cluster you're targeting — provider alias mismatch was a silent root cause for us before (resources looked imported but were bound to a different provider instance).

maria: Good call. Provider aliases are correct. I'll open a short maintenance window and ask app-owner to flip immutable.

sara: If you need, I can help coordinate with the app team and monitor the apply.

maria: Thanks — I'll schedule 10–15m in 30m and post here when it's ready.

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance: staging config update window at 2026-04-01T15:30:00Z — reminder in 20m.

maria: Starting now — removing immutable, re-importing, then re-running `terraform apply`.

maria: Apply succeeded after removing `immutable` and re-importing. Plan no longer shows replace; deployment left intact.

tom: Nice. Can you file a small runbook so app teams know to mark TF-owned configmaps or avoid immutable? :+1:

maria: Will do — adding a note to infra playbook and pinging app teams. Thanks everyone :tada:
